2609.01356.title: Separating Syntax from Language: A Mechanistic Account of Translation in Multilingual LLMs
2609.01356.paper_summary: Multilingual large language models (mLLMs) achieve strong performance in machine translation, yet our understanding of the mechanisms by which they transform representations from one language to another remains incomplete. Prior work suggests that translation decomposes into separable processes within an mLLM, where conceptual content is first represented independently, followed by a production into language-specific form. In this work, we show that translation is even more modular than previously assumed and that the output language production in translation processes is actually further separable into a syntax and a surface language process. We construct controlled multilingual datasets that isolate cross-linguistic differences in word-order and use causal interventions and probing to track how representations are transformed during translation. We find that models first construct target-side word-order before realizing the target language surface form. We identify individual attention heads that are selectively sensitive to syntactic transformations while remaining largely invariant to language identity. These results establish the commitment to a syntactic structure as an independent stage in translation, extending prior decompositions and showing how translation is implemented by functionally different components within mLLMs.
2609.01356.paper_summary_zh: 多語言大型語言模型（mLLMs）在機器翻譯中表現出色，但我們對它們如何將表徵從一種語言轉換到另一種語言的機制的理解仍然不完整。先前的研究表明，翻譯在 mLLM 中分解為可分離的過程，其中概念內容首先獨立表徵，然後轉化為語言特定的形式。在這項工作中，我們顯示翻譯比之前假設的更具模組化，並且翻譯過程中的輸出語言生成實際上可以進一步分解為語法和表面語言過程。我們構建了受控的多語言數據集，以隔離詞序中的跨語言差異，並使用因果干預和探測來追踪在翻譯過程中表徵是如何轉換的。我們發現模型首先構建目標側的詞序，然後才實現目標語言的表面形式。我們識別出對語法轉換具有選擇性敏感的個別注意力頭，同時對語言身份保持大體不變。這些結果確立了語法結構作為翻譯中獨立階段的承諾，擴展了先前的分解，並顯示翻譯是如何由 mLLMs 中功能上不同的組件實現的。
